Non-parametric spatial background surface

Source: R/background_spatial.R
background_spatial.Rd

Estimates the spatial component of the background intensity on a regular grid covering the bounding box of events$region, by summing each event's isotropic Gaussian kernel (using its adaptive bandwidth and edge-correction bg.integral, see add_adaptive_bandwidth() and add_bg_integral()) evaluated at every grid cell, then mean-normalizing over the cells that fall inside region.

Usage

background_spatial(events, cell_size, resp_weight = NULL, chunk_size = 200)

Arguments

events

A semihawkes_events object (from prepare_events()), already passed through add_adaptive_bandwidth() and add_bg_integral() (i.e. events$events$bandwidth and events$events$bg.integral must exist).

cell_size

Grid cell size, in the same linear units as the working CRS (e.g. metres for a UTM projection). There is deliberately no default: pick a value appropriate to your CRS units and the spatial scale of your data (the original script used 150 for a dataset projected in metres).

resp_weight

Optional numeric vector, one value per row of events$events, giving the EM E-step background-responsibility weight for each event. If NULL (the default), every event gets weight 1 (the initial-guess behaviour).

chunk_size

Number of events processed per vectorized chunk, to cap memory use for large datasets and/or fine grids (each chunk builds a n_grid_cells x chunk_size matrix internally). Default 200.

Value

A list of class "semihawkes_spatial_base" with elements:

x, y

The grid's coordinate sequences.

basevalue

length(x) x length(y) matrix, mean-normalized over cells with marks > 0.

marks

length(x) x length(y) integer matrix, 1 where the cell centre falls inside events$region, 0 otherwise.

cell_size

The cell_size used.

fun

A function fun(x, y) that bilinearly interpolates basevalue at arbitrary coordinates via fields::interp.surface(), returning NA outside the grid.

Details

As with temporal_base_weekly(), temporal_base_monthly() and temporal_base_trend(), resp_weight = NULL reproduces the EM initial-guess step (every event contributes with weight 1), and supplying resp_weight (the E-step background-responsibility vector \(\varphi_i\), one value per event) reproduces the weighted re-estimation step.

References

Zhuang, J. and Mateu, J. (2019). A semiparametric spatiotemporal Hawkes-type point process model with periodic background for crime data. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A, 182(3), 919-942.

Examples

ev <- prepare_events(sim_events, sim_region, date_col = "date",
                     end_date = "2022-01-01")
#> The modelled study period ends on 2021-12-29, the day after the last event. `end_date` (2022-01-01) is used only to select events and to label outputs.
ev <- add_adaptive_bandwidth(ev, k = 5, min_dist = 150, min_bandwidth = 300)
ev <- add_bg_integral(ev, n_mc = 500, seed = 1)
bg <- background_spatial(ev, cell_size = 1000)
bg
#> <semihawkes_spatial_base>
#>   grid: 9 x 9 cells (cell_size = 1000), 81 inside `region`
#>   basevalue: mean-normalized over in-region cells (mean = 1.0000)
